title: Subdomain takeover: `devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz` points at a free GitHub Pages name
vulnerability_information:
## Summary

`devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz` is an Expedia-owned hostname that still carries a
CNAME to `eg-internal.github.io`. GitHub Pages answers for that name with "There isn't a GitHub Pages
site here", and the GitHub account `eg-internal` no longer exists — `https://github.com/eg-internal`
returns 404. Both halves of the takeover are therefore open: the DNS record is still published, and
the name it points at is free for anyone to register.

An attacker registers the GitHub username `eg-internal`, creates the repository `eg-internal.github.io`,
and adds the Expedia hostname as a custom domain on that Pages site. GitHub serves the DNS-01 challenge
from the existing record and issues a certificate for
`devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz`, after which the attacker controls content on an
`expedia.biz` hostname over valid HTTPS.

## Evidence (2026-11-03 05:4x UTC, read-only)

```
$ dig +short CNAME devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz
eg-internal.github.io.

$ curl -sS -i http://devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz | head -3
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found


$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz
404          # body: "There isn't a GitHub Pages site here."

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://github.com/eg-internal
404          # the owner name is unregistered -> claimable
```

The 404 from GitHub Pages on the custom hostname is the provider stating that no Pages site owns this
domain. The 404 from `github.com/eg-internal` is the account registry stating that nobody owns the
name the CNAME points at.

## Steps to reproduce (attacker)

1. Register the GitHub account `eg-internal` (free, no verification required to publish Pages).
2. Create repository `eg-internal.github.io`, push any content.
3. Add `devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz` as a custom domain in the repository's
   Pages settings. GitHub's DNS check passes because the CNAME already points at GitHub Pages, and
   ownership verification succeeds because no other Pages site claims the hostname.
4. GitHub provisions a certificate; content is served at
   `https://devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz`.

I have not performed steps 1-4 and will not: no GitHub account was registered for `eg-internal`, no
Pages site was created, and the hostname was not claimed. I am happy to coordinate a controlled
proof-of-claim with a throwaway name if you want a live demonstration.

## Impact

- Attacker-controlled content on an `expedia.biz` hostname with a trusted, provider-issued certificate
  — phishing that passes every padlock and domain-reputation check.
- The hostname's name (`devex-mcp-registry`, `eg-internal`) reads as internal developer tooling, which
  makes a credential-harvesting pretext ("internal MCP registry session expired, sign in with your
  Expedia account") unusually credible to staff.
- Any authorization keyed on the parent domain treats the host as first-party: cookie scoping under
  `.expedia.biz`, CORS allow-lists, `redirect_uri` validation, CSP `connect-src`/`frame-ancestors`
  entries, and SSO-originated redirects.
- Because `ghpages.expedia.biz` appears to be a delegation namespace for GitHub Pages projects, the
  same pattern likely affects sibling records; this one is the instance I could confirm claimable.

## Remediation

1. Remove the CNAME `devex-mcp-registry.eg-internal.ghpages.expedia.biz -> eg-internal.github.io`; or
2. Re-register the `eg-internal` GitHub account/site before someone else does, if the hostname must be
   kept alive.
3. Audit every `*.ghpages.expedia.biz` record against the GitHub owners they point at: a record whose
   owner name is unregistered is claimable today, and one whose owner exists but has no Pages site is
   a latent takeover the moment that account is renamed or deleted.
4. Add "unregister the Pages site and remove the DNS record" to the project-decommission checklist —
   either half left behind is enough to hand the hostname to a stranger.
impact: Takeover of an `expedia.biz` hostname by registering a free GitHub username: attacker content served over a GitHub-issued certificate on an internal-sounding developer hostname, usable for staff phishing and for bypassing parent-domain trust (cookies, CORS, redirect_uri, CSP allow-lists).
